bugs.name: Reopening a pull request removes close history and adds no reopen event
bugs.summary: Reopening a pull request restores Open status but removes the close event and adds no reopen event to the Conversation timeline; the loss remains after refresh.
bugs.expected: After reopening, the pull request should be Open, the Conversation should record the reopen event, and the previously recorded close event should remain visible as history.
bugs.actual: Closing showed `momentic-admin closed this pull request now` and a Closed status. Reopening changed the status to Open, but the close event disappeared and no reopen event appeared. The same timeline remained after refresh.
reproSteps: Start with the authenticated repository-owner account `momentic-admin` (restored using the provided saved authenticated session; no credentials were entered).
At `/`, create and initialize a fresh private repository named `mo-pr-reopen-verify-20260410-r8k2`.
Create branch `feature-pr-reopen-verify-20260410-r8k2` from `main`, add `reopen-test.txt` with a short line of text, and commit it to that branch.
Create a pull request from `feature-pr-reopen-verify-20260410-r8k2` into `main`, titled `PR reopen timeline verification r8k2`.
On `/momentic-admin/mo-pr-reopen-verify-20260410-r8k2/pulls/1`, select Close pull request and observe the Closed badge and the `momentic-admin closed this pull request now` Conversation event.
Select Reopen. Observe that the status returns to Open, while the close event is absent and no reopen event appears in Conversation.
Refresh the same pull request URL and confirm the status is still Open and neither status-change event is present in the visible Conversation timeline.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected the reported expectation as inconsistent with intended behavior. This is an explicit noise-reduction feature, not lost database history. The introducing release note says contradictory timeline actions are canceled and not displayed. The pinned TestCombineOpenClose contains close_open_nullified, with a close followed ten seconds later by reopen and afterCombined=nil. Its next case preserves both comments when reopen occurs after sixty-one seconds. Issue and pull-request conversations share this aggregator. The candidate expects every visible close/reopen event to remain; that expectation directly conflicts with the documented and tested aggregation contract for nearby uninterrupted changes by the same author.
